newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SAYS HAS BROADER ROLE TO PLAY IN LOME.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SAYS HAS BROADER ROLE TO PLAY IN LOME.

text.p: South Africa had a broader role to play in the 70-member Lome Convention with regard to the body's relationship with the European Union, Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom said in Luxembourg on Thursday.

Hanekom said in a speech prepared for delivery during South Africa's signing of its qualified accession to Lome that its new position as member of Lome would be used to protect the interests of all Lome members.
EU foreign ministers agreed in March to allow South Africa to join the Lome Convention -- which groups 70 African, Carribean and Pacific countries in a trade bloc.

"We believe that we have a broader role to play within Lome and that we can make our contribution towards the debate now underway on the wider ACP and European Union relationship after the expiry of the current Lome IV convention," Hanekom said.
Hanekom said South Africa's membership was qualified.
"We had hoped that this would include some form of access to the trade chapter of the Lome Convention in a way that would not harm the interests of the ACP.
"But this was not to be. The Protocol of Accession... excludes us from the trade provisions of the Lome Convention but it does include other important benefits," he said.
Pretoria would be able to participate in ACP and joint ACP/EU institutions while South African companies will be able to tender for European Development Fund projects.
Hanekom said the Lome membership was only one of the tracks of broader negotiations with the EU for a Trade and Development Agreement.
"The parallel bilateral track will include trade and possibly a number of sectoral agreements such as on fisheries and wine and spirits.

"These negotiations are ongoing and we are committed to reaching an agreement which will be beneficial not only to the European Union and South Africa, but also to the southern Africa region," he added.

He urged the EU to move quickly on clarifying the basis on which cumulation provisions in the protocol -- allowing South Africa's neighbours who are also ACP members to use South African inputs in European exports without losing Lome preferences.
"This facility is of considerable potential benefit to the region. It can become an important instrument to encourage greater cross-border co-operation and promote integration".
Agreement on South Africa's membership of Lome became possible after Spain agreed to lift its veto.
Some 40 percent of South Africa's exports go to EU member states and more than one third of its imports are of EU origin.
